patient_information: A 7-year-old girl living in Lima, Peru.
chief_complaint: A chronic skin lesion on her nose.
history_of_present_illness: The lesion appeared 4 months ago as a small nodule and slowly turned into an ulcer, was a bit itchy but not painful, with no history of trauma.
exposure_and_epidemiology: Six months ago, she travelled to a valley on the western slopes of the Andes.
physical_exam: A localized ulcer on the nose, about 2 cm in diameter, with indurated borders and plaque-like infiltration of the surrounding skin; no palpable lymph nodes; rest of physical examination is normal.
labs_and_diagnostics: Microscopic examination of a scraping sample was negative, leishmanin skin test was positive, and PCR was positive, identifying Leishmania (Viannia) peruviana.
differential_diagnosis: Cutaneous leishmaniasis, sporotrichosis, cutaneous tuberculosis, and infection by Balamuthia mandrillaris.
management_and_clinical_course: Treatment began with intravenous sodium stibogluconate (SSG, 20 mg/kg/day for 20 days) and topical imiquimod therapy (every other day for 20 days), resulting in good response after 20 days and no relapse at 3 months follow-up.
final_diagnosis: Cutaneous leishmaniasis caused by Leishmania (Viannia) peruviana.
